answer: A concrete defense is a per-epoch memory-hard liveness audit. Each identity, bonded to a single sable onyx key, must solve a puzzle whose working set is too large to keep many copies resident in one machine RAM, and a rotating jury times the reply. Clones packed on one box contend for the same memory bus, their latencies spike, and the cluster is flagged and slashed. A fleet of N fakes cannot shelter in one harbor of cheap hardware: each needs its own full-bandwidth memory and power, so the attacker pays a linear N times real cost every epoch, not a one-time fee.
